findings.title: Returned SQL fragments have a bare top-level `OR`, so appending `AND …` changes their meaning
findings.description:
The old `WhereInput` objects were safe to compose; the new fragments are not consistently parenthesised.
- **Org and team scope:** `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (lines 171-174) and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` (lines 204-207) return `(A) OR (B)` with no outer parentheses.
- **No-filter path:** `getBaseConditions` returns that fragment unchanged at line 75.
- **Event type filter:** line 106 returns a bare `(…) OR (…)` from the public `getFilterConditions`.

The service's only purpose now is to be embedded as `WHERE ${baseConditions}`. A caller who writes `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}` gets `(team bookings) OR (user bookings AND createdAt >= …)`, so the extra predicate silently skips team bookings. A caller who combines `getAuthorizationConditions()` with their own `OR` can widen the authorization scope.

The behaviour is also inconsistent: when a filter is present the result is `(auth) AND (filter)`, which is safe to extend. Wrap every returned fragment in parentheses.

findings.title: Unreachable branches in `getBaseConditions`, one of them shaped fail-open
findings.description: `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns a non-nullable `Prisma.Sql`, which is always truthy. The `else if (filterConditions) return filterConditions` and the final `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` can therefore never run. The first of these would return filters with no authorization predicate if the auth type were ever made nullable. Reduce it to `filterConditions ? sql\`(${auth}) AND (${filter})\` : auth`.

findings.title: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` loosens the constructor contract and duplicates the zod schema
findings.description:
The constructor previously took the discriminated union inferred from the schema; it now takes a hand-written flat type with `teamId?` (line 58). `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` now compiles, fails `safeParse` at line 62, and silently becomes `options = null`, which yields `1=0`. The caller gets empty results with no error or log, where it used to get a compile error.

The type can also drift from `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema`. If a looser input type is needed, derive it with `z.input<typeof schema>` or keep the union.

findings.title: Test coverage shrank while the code under test stayed
findings.description:
- **Caching:** the whole `Caching` describe block was deleted, but `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` still exist (service lines 83-95). The tests should have been ported, not dropped.
- **`getBaseConditions`:** only the user-scope-plus-filter path is exercised. The no-filter path and the `NOTHING_CONDITION` path are untested.
- **Array binding:** the `= ANY(${number[]})` binding for org and team scope is only compared structurally and never run against Postgres. The user-scope query at lines 481-484 is the only fragment that proves it is valid SQL.
- **Empty team:** the new `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0` branch (service line 200) has no test.

findings.title: Tests assert exact SQL text rather than behaviour
findings.description: `toEqual(Prisma.sql\`…\`)` compares the `strings` and `values` arrays, so a harmless change such as the parenthesisation fix above breaks every assertion. `NOTHING_CONDITION` is also redeclared at line 10 rather than imported, so the test would not notice a mismatch of intent. The org-scope expectation at lines 332-343 relies on the row order of `findMany` calls with no `orderBy` (`team.ts:192`, `membership.ts:409`); this was already true before the change. Running the fragments through `$queryRaw` and asserting on returned rows, as the last test does, would be sturdier.

findings.title: Three hand-rolled `reduce` joins duplicate `Prisma.join`
findings.description: The same reduce-with-index pattern appears at lines 119-122, 171-174 and 204-207. A single helper, or `Prisma.join(conditions.map(c => Prisma.sql\`(${c})\`), " OR ", "(", ")")`, would remove the duplication and add the missing outer parentheses. The comment `// Join all conditions with AND` restates the code.

findings.title: Public `findMany` removed
findings.description: `findMany` was replaced by `getBaseConditions`, which is a breaking API change. A repo-wide search found no callers of `InsightsBookingService` outside its own test, so nothing breaks in this tree.

findings.title: Values are parameterised and column names match the view
findings.description:
Every dynamic value goes through `Prisma.sql` interpolation; there is no `Prisma.raw` or string concatenation. The quoted columns (`userId`, `teamId`, `isTeamBooking`, `eventTypeId`, `eventParentId`) all exist on the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` view (`packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1682-1708`).

Semantics match the old code:
- `teamIds` always contains `orgId`, so `ANY` never receives an empty array.
- Omitting the user clause for an empty team is equivalent to the old `in: []`.
- `1=0` replaces `{ id: -1 }` as the deny-all condition.
- The `isOrgOwnerOrAdmin` rewrite at line 217 is behaviour-preserving.
